1: Some professionals deliver successful projects. Others leave a lasting mark on the people, standards and industries around them.
2: Honorary Fellow of the Project Controls Institute… is a board-conferred recognition for distinguished professional contribution, leadership and service.
3: It involves NO examination — and is separate from P-C-I's examined certifications. Every application is considered individually… and recognition is conferred solely at the Board's discretion.
4: It is intended for experienced leaders… whose impact spans project controls, cost engineering, finance, project management, or a closely related discipline.
5: Applicants come from infrastructure, energy, technology, aviation, project finance, government and academia. And every sector where strong professional leadership shapes OUTCOMES.
6: To be considered, applicants need at least eight years of relevant experience… including three at managerial level. And a demonstrable record of distinguished contribution. Meeting these criteria does not guarantee recognition.
7: Applicants provide a professional profile, résumé, qualifications, career history and evidence of contribution… for confidential review. P-C-I charges no nomination, assessment or credential fee.
8: Those selected are recognised as an Honorary Fellow — recorded so anyone can verify it at source… and labelled honorary, never a passed examination. Accepted applicants may also receive access to selected P-C-I learning resources, subject to programme terms.
9: You may also indicate whether your contribution aligns with project controls, project finance, or project management.
10: If your leadership has advanced the profession… your contribution deserves consideration. Apply for Honorary Fellow P-C-I at… P-C-I-A-I dot org.
